questions.question_text: You have been tasked with creating a file share in Azure Files for your company's shared documents. Which of the following steps should you perform first?

options.label: B
options.text: Configure the file share access permissions.

options.label: C
options.text: Mount the file share on a virtual machine.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable soft delete for the file share.

questions.explanation: The first step in creating a file share in Azure Files is to create a storage account. This storage account will host the file share and allow you to configure additional settings and permissions.

questions.question_text: How can you configure Azure Blob Storage to automatically move data to a cooler tier based on the last modified date?

options.label: B
options.text: Set up a blob lifecycle management policy.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a new blob container with a cooler default tier.

questions.explanation: Blob lifecycle management policies allow you to define rules that automatically transition blobs to different access tiers, such as moving data to a cooler tier based on the last modified date.

questions.question_text: Which feature must be enabled to restore deleted blobs to their previous state within a specified retention period?
questions.explanation: Enabling soft delete for containers allows you to restore deleted blobs to their previous state within the retention period specified, helping to protect against accidental deletions.

questions.question_text: Your organization wants to protect file share data from accidental deletion. Which feature should you enable to achieve this?

options.label: C
options.text: Enable soft delete for Azure Files.

options.label: D
options.text: Use Microsoft Entra ID for authentication.

questions.explanation: Enabling soft delete for Azure Files allows you to recover file shares that have been accidentally deleted, thus providing an additional layer of data protection.
